title: SRD coverage: mundane land animals
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 33 land-animal identities issue #37 enumerates. The SRD supplies the creature identity each record answers to and nothing else: no SRD statistics, wording or presentation is reproduced, and no third-party GURPS conversion was used as an input. Every trait comes from the controlled vocabulary in scripts/srd/trait-library.mjs, which carries the published page reference and cost for each entry, so a reviewer can check a build against the rules rather than against this file's assertions. Typical Stats, damage, point totals and ratings are derived from the trait list at build time and are never authored here.

monsters.name: Bear, Black
monsters.lair: A hollow log, rock cleft or dug-out den under a fallen tree, used for winter sleep and for raising cubs.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A stocky forest bear that climbs better than it fights and would much rather rob a camp than face one. It reads a clearing by scent long before it sees anybody, and most encounters end with it ambling away. A sow with cubs is the exception. She closes fast and swats with both forepaws, and she will not bluff twice.
provenanceNotes: Enhanced Move covers the short charge; a black bear does not sustain that pace.

monsters.name: Bear, Brown
monsters.lair: A dug hillside den above the snow line, reused season after season and defended on sight.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Half again the weight of a black bear, with none of its willingness to withdraw. A brown bear stands to look over cover, drops, and covers the ground between in three strides. The hump of muscle across its shoulders is built for digging; a single swipe carries a season of that behind it.

monsters.name: Bear, Polar
monsters.lair: A snow den scraped into a drift or pressure ridge; a hunting bear keeps no fixed home at all.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: The one bear that hunts people on purpose. It crosses open ice at a walk, yellow-white against white, and swims stretches of freezing water that would kill whatever it is following. The cold does not slow it. A camp on the ice is a larder that cannot get far.

monsters.name: Boar
monsters.lair: A trampled wallow in dense thorn scrub, rooted bare and stinking, with escape runs cut through the brush.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Delivered on a charge, low and upward.

monsters.description: A barrel of gristle on short legs, armored across the shoulders by a shield of hardened hide it grows for fighting other boars. There is no posturing first. A boar that has made up its mind comes in low and straight, and the tusks go up under whatever they meet.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Camel
monsters.lair: None; a camel keeps to its caravan lines and the wells its handlers know.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: A camel bites to settle arguments, including with its own driver.

monsters.description: A long-legged pack animal built for ground that kills horses, carrying its own water and shrugging off heat, glare and blown sand behind a second eyelid. It is unhurried and enormously strong for its frame. It is also thoroughly bad-tempered: it spits, it bites, and it remembers who deserved it.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Cat
monsters.lair: A barn loft, a warm hearthstone, or whatever roof cavity has the best view of the rats.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Too small to threaten anybody and far too quiet to keep out. A house cat crosses a room without a sound, lands from heights that ought to hurt, and fits through gaps its shoulders say it should not. At a table it is a witness and a nuisance rather than an opponent.

monsters.name: Cheetah
monsters.lair: A shaded scrape in tall grass where cubs are left while the mother hunts.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Aimed at the throat once the quarry is down.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Used to trip a running target rather than to wound. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: The fastest thing on four legs, and the least able to keep it up. A cheetah stalks to within a hundred yards, then spends everything it has in a few seconds, knocking its quarry off its feet at the end of the run. Caught at that moment it is exhausted and light-boned, and it will give up the kill rather than fight for it.
provenanceNotes: Enhanced Move models the sprint. A cheetah that has run flat out is winded and disengages rather than fighting.

Rating caveat for review: the CER path credits Move linearly, so the sprint alone contributes 18 of this record's offense rating and lands it beside a lion. At the table a cheetah is much the lesser fight. Either the encounter weight or the sprint's accessibility should carry the correction; this build does not pre-empt that decision.

monsters.name: Death Dog
monsters.lair: A fouled dry wash or ruin littered with the picked-over remains of travelers.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Anyone bitten rolls HT. On a failure the wound will not close: it goes gray at the edges and spreads, costing 1 HP a day until the rot is cured by magic or by cutting well past the margin. The lost HP does not return until the disease is stopped.

monsters.description: A two-headed hound the color of dust, running the dry country in pairs and hating everything that walks upright. Both heads bite and both heads watch, so there is no blind side to approach from. What kills travelers is rarely the wound. It is what grows in the wound afterwards, slowly and visibly, and it does not stop on its own.
provenanceNotes: The disease is priced as a 30-point disabling ability, so the rating counts it rather than reading the dog as a weak biter.

monsters.name: Deer
monsters.lair: A bed of flattened bracken in thick cover, changed nightly.

traits.note: Stags only; hinds have the hooves and nothing else.

attacks.name: Antlers
attacks.notes: Stags in season only.

monsters.description: Woodland game, and the reason a forest encounter table is not all teeth. A deer hears a party long before it sees one and leaves at a speed nothing on foot will match. A stag in season, cornered, is a genuine hazard. The rest of the year it simply runs.
provenanceNotes: Encounter weight is high on purpose: this is the most common thing a party meets in temperate woodland.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Dire Wolf
monsters.lair: A cave mouth or undercut bank fouled with bone, held by the whole pack.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: A dire wolf bites low and drives, trying to put its target on the ground for the rest of the pack.

monsters.description: A wolf grown to the size of a pony, hunting in packs that work a treeline the way soldiers work a hedgerow. They circle, they cut off the slowest, and they take turns. One is a serious fight. Four have already picked somebody.
notes: The pack is the threat. Run these as a coordinated group, not as four separate rolls.

monsters.name: Dog
monsters.lair: A yard, a doorway, or the lee side of whatever building feeds it.
monsters.description: The ordinary working dog of farm and street: forty pounds of noise and nose. On its own it is barely a combatant, and what it is for is warning, tracking and company. Village strays run in loose packs and will follow a party for miles on the chance of scraps.
provenanceNotes: Statistics describe a small working or village dog. Larger war and hunting breeds should be built separately.

monsters.name: Donkey
monsters.lair: None; a donkey belongs to whatever holding or caravan owns its lead rope.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Only when it has no way out.

monsters.description: Short, patient and surefooted, carrying a third of its own weight up tracks a horse would refuse. It eats what it finds, drinks little, and stops dead when it judges the next step unsafe. Handlers call that stubbornness. More of them have been saved by it than killed by it.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Elephant
monsters.lair: None; a herd walks a circuit between water and forage and holds no fixed ground.

attacks.name: Trample
attacks.notes: Against a target already down.

attacks.name: Trunk
attacks.notes: Also used to grab and throw.

monsters.description: Seven tons of animal that is not remotely stupid, moving in a family group led by the oldest cow. Left alone it ignores people entirely. Provoked, or separated from a calf, it comes forward at a speed nothing that size should manage, and it does not need the tusks to settle the argument.
provenanceNotes: The trunk is a fine manipulator, so this build drops No Fine Manipulators from the quadruped set.

monsters.name: Elk
monsters.lair: Open woodland edge and high meadow; the herd beds where it grazes.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Front hooves, brought down on a target that has gone down.

monsters.description: A deer the size of a horse, carrying a rack wide enough to catch on branches. Out of season it is meat that runs away. In the rut a bull is loud, sleepless and looking for something to fight, and a party crossing his meadow will do.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Badger
monsters.lair: A dug sett of packed earth tunnels with several bolt holes, extended every year.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Digging claws, as long as a knife. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Low, wide and built entirely out of bad attitude, with digging claws that go through packed earth and will do the same to a boot. It would rather be underground than anywhere else. A party that opens up its sett gets everything the badger has, immediately, without a warning growl.

monsters.name: Giant Boar
monsters.lair: A wallow the size of a cart, ringed by uprooted saplings and churned mud.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Tusks the length of a forearm, driven upward on the charge.

monsters.description: A boar the size of a plow horse, with hide over the shoulders that turns a spear point and a temper that has never once improved. It charges the moment it is sure, keeps going through the first wound, and is generally still coming when whoever stood the ground has reconsidered.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Elk
monsters.lair: Deep old forest and high valleys, far from any road.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Against a target already down.

monsters.description: Rare enough that seeing one counts as a sign rather than a sighting. It stands taller at the shoulder than a mounted rider, moves through heavy timber without hurrying, and watches a party with something closer to judgement than fear. Killing one is legal almost nowhere and forgiven almost never.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Goat
monsters.lair: Ledges and scree above the tree line, on ground nothing else will stand on.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Delivered downhill wherever possible.

monsters.description: An ill-tempered mountain goat the size of a pony, standing on ledges that have no business holding it. Hill folk keep them for milk and haulage and put up with the bruises. In the wild they defend a slope by ramming, and on bad footing the fall afterwards is worse than the hit.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Hyena
monsters.lair: A den under a thorn thicket or ruin, floored with splintered bone.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Jaws built to crack marrow bone; armor straps and shield rims fare no better.

monsters.description: Shoulder-high, sloped from front to back, and loud in the dark. Giant hyenas run in clans and are as happy taking a kill off something else as making their own. They will follow a caravan for days without closing, waiting for somebody to fall behind. The jaws go through bone as a matter of routine.

monsters.name: Giant Weasel
monsters.lair: A stolen burrow or root cavity, taken from whatever dug it and ate first.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Long canines, aimed at the neck and held on.

monsters.description: A weasel grown to the length of a man, all spine and appetite, pouring through gaps too small to crawl through and seeing perfectly well in a lightless tunnel. Strength is not the point. It reaches the throat first and does not let go.

monsters.name: Goat
monsters.lair: A byre, a hillside pen, or wherever the rope broke.
monsters.description: Livestock, sacrifice, and the single most escape-prone animal any village owns. A goat eats what is left, climbs what it should not, and butts anybody who bends over near it. As an encounter it is scenery. As a plot device it is whatever the party tied it to and forgot.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Horse, Heavy
monsters.lair: A stable or picket line; a heavy horse is property, not wildlife.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Shod rear hooves; a connecting kick breaks what it lands on.

monsters.description: The plow and wagon horse: heavy through the chest, slow to startle, strong enough to drag a loaded cart out of a flooded ford. It is not a fighting animal and will not carry anybody into a fight. It hauls what an expedition cannot and it eats accordingly.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Horse, Light
monsters.lair: A stable, a paddock, or a picket line outside an inn.
monsters.description: The ordinary riding horse: fast over roads, willing under a light load, and entirely unwilling to hold its ground when something roars. Untrained for war, it shies, bolts or throws its rider — worth remembering before a party gallops into anything.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Lion
monsters.lair: A shaded kopje or thicket the pride returns to between hunts.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Closes on the throat and holds.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A pride hunts in daylight when it suits and at night when it does not. The lionesses do the work, spread wide through grass that hides them completely until the last twenty yards, and the male arrives afterwards to take what he wants. A single lion is manageable. A pride is a flanking maneuver.

monsters.name: Mammoth
monsters.lair: None; the herd follows forage across tundra and cold steppe.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Curved tusks longer than a spear.

attacks.name: Trample
attacks.notes: Against a target already down.

monsters.description: An elephant rebuilt for a country that freezes solid: shag-haired, high-shouldered, tusks sweeping forward until they cross. The cold does nothing to it. Herds are dangerous by accident and lethal on purpose, and the tribes that hunt them do it from a distance, with everybody they have.

monsters.name: Mule
monsters.lair: None; a mule belongs to a pack train.

attacks.name: Kick
attacks.notes: A mule kicks sideways and backwards, and its aim is better than anyone expects.

monsters.description: The pack animal of choice anywhere a cart cannot go: stronger than a donkey, tougher than a horse, and impossible to talk into a bad idea. It carries an expedition's load up switchbacks all day, refuses a single step onto rotten ground, and kicks whoever insists.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Panther
monsters.lair: A fork in a heavy branch above a game trail, with a kill stored in it.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: A black leopard that hunts from above and is not seen beforehand. It works the canopy over a trail, drops onto whoever is walking last, and is back up the trunk with the body before the front of the column has turned around. The silence is most of the danger.

monsters.name: Pony
monsters.lair: A byre or hill pasture.
monsters.description: A small, shaggy, hard-wearing horse that carries a halfling or a child comfortably and a grown adventurer badly. It lives outdoors year-round on poor grazing, keeps its footing on hill tracks, and is the mount most parties can actually afford.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger
monsters.lair: A rock shelter above a herd trail, floored with the ribs of things much larger than a person.

attacks.name: Sabre Teeth
attacks.notes: Two blades of tooth, driven down into the neck once the target is pinned.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Used to hold the target still. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Heavier and slower than a tiger, and built for one job: putting something enormous on the ground and opening its throat with a pair of teeth as long as daggers. It cannot run anything down. It has already spent an hour getting close enough that it does not have to.

monsters.name: Tiger
monsters.lair: A den in dense cover near water, at the center of a territory it patrols alone.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Solitary, striped into invisibility against broken shade, and willing to swim a river to reach something worth eating. A tiger stalks to a distance it can cross in one rush and does not commit until it can. The first anyone knows of it is usually the person beside them being gone.

monsters.name: Warhorse, Heavy
monsters.lair: A stable, and a groom who knows better than to walk behind it.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Trained to strike forward on command rather than only to kick out behind.

monsters.description: A destrier: bred heavy, trained not to shy from fire, steel or screaming, and taught to fight from under a rider. It costs more than most people's houses and earns it, because it will carry a charge home into a line that is trying very hard to stop it. On the ground it is foul-tempered.
notes: The light warhorse the 3.5 corpus prints separately is this record ridden lighter; use the same statistics and drop the barding.
provenanceNotes: Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Wolf
monsters.lair: A dug den under a bank or root ball, used only while there are pups.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Wolves bite and pull backwards, working to drag a target off its feet.

monsters.description: Alone, a wolf is a nervous dog with better teeth. In a pack it is a method: they test a party for a mile, find who tires, and then commit all at once from three sides. Winter packs are larger, hungrier and far less careful about what counts as prey.

monsters.name: Wolverine
monsters.lair: A snow tunnel or rock crevice, marked and reeking.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Thirty pounds of animal that drives bears off their kills, and does it by being completely unwilling to stop. A wolverine that has committed keeps clawing through wounds that should have ended it, and there is no way to end the fight except to kill it.
